problem: VLN is evaluated as a one-way task, but robots may need to return to the start; a policy such as NaVILA drops from 40.0% standalone one-way success to 22.0% when the same route is run as the Return leg of a continuous round trip. Prior work assumes that more accurate information (memory, localisation) automatically yields correct behaviour.
motivation: Practical robots must return after inspection or retrieval, and the just-executed Outbound route is a free spatial prior. The paper separates information quality from behavioural consistency and online reliability by comparing Oracle and online versions of the same interfaces.
key_idea: Record the executed Outbound path as sparse geometric LiDAR anchors and query them in reverse through a structured hint, action-level arbitration, and terminal verification, gated online by learned, calibrated reliability estimates, while NaVILA remains the primary controller.
insight: Exact information delivered only as a text hint gives a non-significant gain (22.0 to 37.2%, p=0.18). The large gains appear only when the reference can act on the policy output (arbitration: 70.5%) and constrain termination (86.0%). Online, relocalisation confidence is below threshold at 62% of Return steps, so the hint and arbiter are withheld there. The remaining gap to Oracle is thus caused by unreliable geometric evidence, not weak interfaces. A geometry-only route follower without the VLM gets only 23.9%, so the route memory should support the policy rather than replace it.
method: Continuous round-trip protocol: reverse-paired human instructions from the same scene, no reset between Outbound and Return; Return is scored as distance to the Outbound start s0 (3.0 m radius, valid STOP required).

Sparse route memory: during Outbound, an anchor (2-D LiDAR scan, index, cumulative distance, relative transform) is created every 1.0 m (max 512 points, 0.10 m voxel). The memory is frozen after Outbound and queried in reverse order.

Online registration and reliability: multi-seed 2-D ICP against candidate anchors, updating the route state only with topology, multi-frame and ambiguity support. A gradient-boosted model with Platt calibration predicts pose, bearing and distance reliability (thresholds 0.70/0.68/0.74, joint AND gate).

Structured route hint (D1): a fixed-template text appended to the instruction giving target anchor, bearing (ahead/left/right), distance and remaining progress. It is withheld when relocalisation confidence is under 0.90.

Hint-Action arbitration (D2): overrides the NaVILA action when it conflicts with the reliable bearing class (forward vs turn conflict at 30°) and a 1.0x0.84 m LiDAR corridor confirms traversability. Disabled within 0.35 m of the anchor.

Terminal verification (D3): treats STOP as a request and checks distance, start-anchor support and approach trend. It accepts, vetoes, defers, or forces STOP when the robot is inside the start region.
Stuck recovery (online only): after 8 queries with under 0.15 m displacement it turns about 180°, drives forward, and re-faces the next anchor.

setting.backbone: NaVILA (8-bit, frozen VLA policy) plus a gradient-boosted reliability model with Platt calibration
setting.training_data: NaVILA used as is; the reliability GBM is trained on registration features (data scale not stated in the text)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB for NaVILA plus 2-D LiDAR for anchors and registration; dead-reckoned route-state prior
setting.action_space: low-level discrete legged locomotion commands (forward/left/right) for a Unitree Go2
setting.privileged: none for the online system; the Oracle variants use simulator pose for anchor bearing and distance

numbers.eval_set_note: M50: 50 reverse-paired episodes selected from 264 candidates for high Outbound reliability; SR_ret is conditional on Outbound success (49 episodes)
numbers.extra: online 2-D ICP; success radius 3.0 m to start s0; stuck recovery enabled
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Reliability-aware online, 49 Outbound episodes, AR_ret 59.2, SR_ret 55.1 (n=31 subset 61.3)

numbers.extra: anchor bearing and distance from simulator pose (privileged)

numbers.backbone: deterministic reverse-polyline follower with ICP route state
numbers.extra: stuck recovery disabled; terminal verification retained
numbers.evidence: the geometry-only follower succeeds on only 11/46=23.9%

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; all results are on the authors' own M50 round-trip cohort. The split label val-unseen is an approximation.
results: Online reliability-aware route memory raises Return success from 22.0% (language-only NaVILA) to 55.1% (p=0.0015 on 49 common episodes). The Oracle ceiling is 86.0%, above the 40% standalone one-way rate. The online system beats geometry-only route following (54.3% vs 23.9% on 46 common episodes, p=0.009) but is 26.2 paired points below full Oracle.
limitations: Simulation only, one robot (Go2), one base policy (NaVILA) and one hint template; no real-robot tests.
Small cohort (M50, selected for high Outbound reliability, ~40 paired episodes per contrast), which leaves the terminal increment underpowered; run-to-run non-determinism changes Outbound outcomes.
The joint AND reliability gate is not separated per operation, no no-gate control is run, and the geometry-only baseline also disables stuck recovery.
